items.stem: You want to pull an item description into a transactions table from an item master, returning blank when no match is found. Which approach is most robust in current Excel?

options.text: XLOOKUP with an 'if not found' argument
options.rationale: Correct: XLOOKUP has a built-in if-not-found argument and does not depend on column position.

options.text: VLOOKUP with the item column to the right of the key
options.rationale: VLOOKUP cannot look to the left of the key and has no native not-found argument.
Manual copying breaks as data changes.

options.text: Hard-coding descriptions in the transaction rows
options.rationale: Hard-coding duplicates data and cannot be maintained.

items.explanation: Correct: XLOOKUP has a built-in if-not-found argument and is not tied to column position.

items.stem: Which TWO quantities does a classic reorder point depend on? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: the reorder point covers expected demand over the lead time.
Correct: safety stock buffers demand and lead-time variability.
An invoice number is reference data, not a reorder input.

options.text: The colour of the product label
options.rationale: Label colour is irrelevant to reorder calculation.

items.explanation: Correct: a reorder point equals expected demand over the lead time plus safety stock.

items.stem: In ABC analysis, what characterises 'A' items?

options.text: A small number of SKUs accounting for a large share of value
options.rationale: Correct: A items are the vital few that drive most of the value.

options.text: The cheapest items by unit cost
options.rationale: ABC ranks by total value contribution, not unit cost.

options.text: Items with the longest supplier lead time
options.rationale: Lead time is not the ABC criterion.

options.text: Items stored at the back of the warehouse
options.rationale: Physical location is not the ABC criterion.

items.explanation: Correct: A items are the small share of SKUs that account for most of the inventory value.
